title: bursera simaruba
intro: Bursera simaruba, commonly known as West Indian birch or gumbo-limbo, is a tropical tree species belonging to the family Burseraceae. This plant has been used in traditional medicine for its various health benefits, including the treatment of fever, rheumatism, and skin conditions, such as eczema and dermatitis. The therapeutic actions of Bursera simaruba include anti-inflammatory, antibacterial, and antifungal properties, which contribute to its effectiveness in wound healing and skin care. The bioactive constituents of this plant include flavonoids, phenolic acids, and terpenoids, which are responsible for its medicinal properties.
